{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZW1XgA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC-LHI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 61, "title": "Add skippable staged PC-VAN session entry without collecting credentials", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `44b404b057c5a456d8f6154cb81c7ccff3de7579`, initial connection and RECONNECT show a short connection status and then MAIN. They omit service identification, authentication presentation, session-date lines and the profile stage visible in a preserved 1995 PC-VAN session. This affects every visit.

This is an extension of the completed connection scope, not a demonstrated regression from the latest library/OSL merge.

## Expected outcome

Provide a short, automatically progressing, skippable entry sequence: connection status → service identification → scripted fictional ID/password presentation → previous-end/current-start dates → scripted profile decline → concise original welcome notice → MAIN.

The sequence is presentation only. It must not request credentials, perform authentication, create an account or require a human handle. Preserve optional local handle registration as a separate existing workflow.

## Context

Implementation inspected at the baseline:

- [src/connection.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/44b404b057c5a456d8f6154cb81c7ccff3de7579/src/connection.ts): `completeConnection()` immediately returns the navigation welcome; commands cancel the wait.
- [src/main.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/44b404b057c5a456d8f6154cb81c7ccff3de7579/src/main.ts): a 1.2-second timer, Escape and command submission converge on connection completion, which queues `commands.welcome()`.
- `src/commands.ts` owns the optional local registration prompts. `src/terminal.ts` owns output reveal, IME guards and keyboard input. `src/storage/repository.ts` already records actual login/logout times.

Historical basis, inspected 2026-10-23:

- [Preserved session published in 2010, dated 1995-04-02](https://akibabara.com/blog/4569.html): shows identification, ID/password stages, previous-use-end/current-use-start dates and a profile question. Confidence is high about the preserved excerpt's contents, moderate about independent authenticity and adjacent-year applicability. It is incomplete and does not establish the entire 1996 sequence.
- [Client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html): explicitly describes reading an announcement immediately after login. Its release date and exact host interaction remain unverified; this supports an announcement concept, not copied wording or an authenticated sequence.
- [Retrospective screen reproductions](https://paradisearmy.com/doujin/pasok3pc-van.htm): keep its 1992 login example separate from the selected circa-1996 MAIN reproduction. The older announcement prompt cannot establish 1996 controls.
- [Newsletter dated 1996-11-25, printed page 12](https://www.mimi-hp.normanet.ne.jp/MIMI312.pdf): the profile question follows a connection from PC-VAN into NORMA and precedes NORMA's own MAIN. This is a different service context; do not transplant its gateway commands, password or menus into root login. PDF text was readable through the alternative `www` hostname; page-image retrieval failed.

Reconstruction decision: use original concise Japanese text, a fixed fictional demonstration identity and scripted password/profile stages. Do not implement unsupported profile-editor branches or invent authentication errors. Timing, notice wording and exact 1996 applicability remain reconstructed. Keep provenance in existing About/Details and research documentation, following [completed Issue #31](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/31).

For this increment, session-date lines represent actual browser-session timestamps using the existing UTC convention. Do not silently change their year to 1996. Disclose this limitation on demand; a service-wide historical display calendar remains separate work.

Duplication and validation evidence: live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs and no matching staged-entry work. [Completed Issue #9](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/9) established the brief connection effect, history and logs. [PR #60](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/60) and `docs/validation.md` report 213 passing tests and a successful production build for the preceding work. These are existing Coordinator records; this research graph ran no application checks.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Initial entry and Q → RECONNECT present the ordered stages above and reach the unchanged MAIN automatically. Use a short bounded duration and disclose its reconstruction; no indefinite waits or mandatory new interaction.
- [ ] Authentication and profile handling are scripted output, never credential-entry prompts. Use an invented identity independent of stored human/member IDs, no real password, no authentication requests and no new account records. The profile stage takes the scripted decline path without advertising unsupported interactive branches as functional.
- [ ] Date lines distinguish previous logout from current login. A fresh world has no invented previous logout; reload without Q does not fabricate one. Preserve actual stored timestamps, history, activity scheduling and backup compatibility. Reuse existing session records without a schema migration.
- [ ] Escape skips the remaining entry from every stage and remains safe when repeated. Returning-user commands submitted during entry cancel it and execute exactly once. Preserve instant/reduced-motion behavior, pending input, IME guards and output reveal. No timer may later print login stages into a service or human prompt.
- [ ] Run the existing optional registration invitation only at the completed-entry handoff and at most once under its existing rules. Preserve register/decline, reading without a handle, pending WRITE/REPLY registration and composer ownership. Timer, Escape and rapid submission races must not duplicate invitations, MAIN output or session bookkeeping.
- [ ] Preserve Settings access and focus behavior during entry, existing Q scoping, reconnect history and navigation. Repeated completion callbacks are harmless; HELP/BACK after entry do not replay it.
- [ ] Add focused controller and production-browser coverage using existing Playwright facilities: natural automatic entry without the startup skip helper; fresh and returning worlds; previous-logout handling; skip at intermediate stages; early commands; rapid/repeated completion; delayed startup data; and repeated Q/reconnect. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, IME, terminal, composition, mail and OLT coverage. Adjust startup helpers only where necessary, retaining explicit tests of the unskipped journey.
- [ ] Update README, existing About/Details and research documentation with source dates, confidence, stage assumptions, actual-date policy and NORMA's separate scope. Routine terminal output stays concise and contains no provenance paragraphs or source URLs. Do not copy archived identities, messages or a complete transcript.
- [ ] Run the documented `npm test` workflow before merge; its configuration includes TypeScript checking and the production build. Check changed documentation links and whitespace, inspect the final diff and record actual results and skipped checks. No new framework, model download or hardware check is needed.

## Optional validation

Automated desktop/narrow screenshots may help assess readability. Further dated root-login evidence may refine wording or order later. Historical-user feedback and physical terminal testing are optional, not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
